name: example taxonomy
_comment: A deliberately small, generic example so the library and its tests have
something to run against. It is not a real taxonomy for any particular
When you write a real one: key off document KIND only. Do not encode a
document store's folder tree here. Such a tree gets restructured, and a
taxonomy that mirrors it would be wrong the week after it was written.

letter.what: A piece of correspondence addressed from one party to another: a letter, a memo, or a printed email.
letter.not_for: A form, an invoice, or a report that merely happens to be attached to a letter.
examples: Dear Mr Smith, further to our meeting on the 14th...
a printed email chain with From/To/Subject headers

covering_letter.what: A short letter whose purpose is to introduce or transmit something enclosed with it.
covering_letter.not_for: A letter that makes its own substantive point rather than introducing an enclosure.
examples: Please find enclosed the signed contract.
I attach the report you requested.

chasing_letter.what: A letter asking for something that is late or outstanding.
chasing_letter.not_for: A first request; this is specifically a follow-up.
examples: We wrote to you on 3 March and have not yet had a reply.
This account is now 60 days overdue.

financial_document.what: A document stating amounts of money owed, paid or quoted: an invoice, a credit note, a quotation or a statement.
financial_document.not_for: A letter that discusses money without itself being the financial record.
examples: Statement of account as at 31 March

invoice.what: A demand for payment for goods or services already supplied.
invoice.not_for: A quotation, which offers a price for work not yet done.
examples: Invoice number, invoice date, payment terms, a total due

quotation.what: An offer of a price for work not yet carried out.
quotation.not_for: An invoice, which bills for work already done.
examples: Quotation ref Q-2291, valid for 30 days

credit_note.what: A document reducing or cancelling an amount previously invoiced.
credit_note.not_for: An invoice, which increases what is owed.

technical_record.what: A record of technical work, equipment or measurements: a test sheet, a schedule of equipment, a commissioning record, a set of readings.
technical_record.not_for: A narrative report about technical work; this is the record itself, usually tabular or form-shaped.
examples: a table of set points and measured values with pass/fail columns
a schedule of equipment with model numbers and serial numbers

form.what: A blank or filled-in form: labelled fields, boxes, or a printed template to be completed.
form.not_for: A table of results, which is a technical_record.
examples: a printed application form with tick boxes
